title: The Tunguska Event
hook: In June 1908, a massive explosion ripped through Siberia's Taiga, flattening thousands of square kilometres - yet investigators never found a crater.

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: On 30 June 1908, a bright fireball detonated over the Tunguska River.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: Witnesses reported a flash brighter than the sun, followed by a powerful shockwave.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: The blast flattened about 2,150 square kilometres of forest, uprooting trees radially.

beats.label: CLUE 3
beats.line: Expeditions in 1927 found no crater, only scorched earth and standing stumps.

beats.label: THEORY
beats.line: One theory suggests the event was caused by a meteoroid airburst, similar to modern Chelyabinsk.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: Tree-ring studies show a high-energy blast, yet no fragments were recovered.

end.line: What caused the sky fire that left no crater?

description: Explore the 1908 Tunguska explosion that flattened Siberian forest without leaving a crater.

facts.claim: The Tunguska explosion occurred on 30 June 1908 over the Tunguska River in Siberia.
Eyewitnesses described a flash brighter than the sun and a powerful shockwave.
The blast flattened roughly 2,150 square kilometres of forest.
Expeditions in 1927 found no impact crater, only scorched earth and standing trees.
The leading hypothesis is that a meteoroid airburst caused the event, similar to the 2013 Chelyabinsk meteor.
Tree-ring analysis indicates a high-energy explosion, but no fragments have been recovered.
